chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who seeks the pleasure of the people with what Angers Allah, his praise from the people would be a condemnation; and the one who pursues the obedience of Allah by angering the people, Allah would Suffice him for the animosity of every enemy, and the envy of every envious one, and the rebellion of every rebel, and Allah Mighty and Majestic would be a Helper for him and a Backer'.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of seeking people's pleasure by disobeying God?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni uses this hadith to establish the principle of 'Istiqamah' (steadfastness) in the face of social pressure, a key theme in Shia ethical jurisprudence. It highlights the paradox that compromising divine command for human approval leads to inevitable social instability, whereas prioritizing God's pleasure guarantees divine protection from the 'adversity of every adversary.' This serves as a practical guide for believers navigating the tension between communal harmony and religious integrity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who seeks the pleasure of the people with what Angers Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, his praise from the people would be a condemnation; and the one who pursues the obedience of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> by angering the people, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Suffice him for the animosity of every enemy, and the envy of every envious one, and the rebellion of every rebel, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would be a Helper for him and a Backer’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from ‘ Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever seeks the pleasure of people with that which angers Allah, the people praising will belittle him. Whoever gives preference to Allah’s obedience with that which angers people, Allah will suffice him against the animosity of every enemy, the envy of all enviers and the transgression of all transgressors. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will be his helper and supporter.’”
